person.persName: الاشي علي بن عثمان بن محمد سراج الدين الفرغاني
al-Ūšī, ʻAlī b. ʻUṯmān b. Muḥammad b. Sulaymān Sirāǧ al-Dīn al-Taymī al-Farġānī
person.floruit: 6th/12th centuryḤanafī scholar from Ūš in Farġāna of the 6th/12th century. Nothing is known about his life. He is known specially for his lāmiyya, a theological poem of 66 or 68 lines also called Badʾ al-amālī and Qaṣīdat Yaqūlu al-'Abd . It contains a simple creed in the Ḥanafī tradition close to Māturīdī doctrine and seems influenced by the ʿAqāʾid of Abū Ḥafṣ al-Nasafī. The Muʿtazila are explicitly condemned, while criticism of Ašʿarī doctrine is muted. The reality of miracles worked by Ṣūfī saints is upheld, but prophets are ranked in excellence above saints. Among the numerous commentaries written on the poem, that of ʿAlī al-Qārī al-Harawī (d. 1014/1605) is the mostpopular.
